subject.title: [Bug]: MidTurnPrecheckSignal leaks error to UI via pushLoopFailure before internal retry completes

question: Which boundary should own suppression of non-terminal mid-turn precheck control-flow failures before this issue is closed?
rationale: The source-level bug is clear, but the linked fix crosses the embedded-runner and reusable agent-core boundary, so automation should not choose the permanent contract shape without maintainer intent.

options.title: Review the linked PR boundary
options.body: Use the linked PR as the active candidate, decide whether its generic sentinel contract is acceptable, and request proof or adjustments before merge.

options.title: Keep recovery embedded-runner-owned
options.body: Ask for a replacement shape that catches or prevents the signal inside the embedded runner so agent-core remains unaware of this recovery detail.

options.title: Define an agent-core contract
options.body: Accept a generic agent-core control-flow-error seam only if maintainers want reusable callers to declare selected thrown errors as non-failure control flow.

recommendation.title: Review the linked PR boundary
recommendation.body: Use the linked PR as the active candidate, decide whether its generic sentinel contract is acceptable, and request proof or adjustments before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent merger of adjacent compaction/precheck recovery work and a good routing candidate for the agent-core versus embedded-runner boundary choice.
